newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal invites Chinese investment in power, tourism.
newsitem.headline: Nepal invites Chinese investment in power, tourism.

text.p: Nepal on Wednesday invited Chinese investment in the Himalayan kingdom's hydro-electric power, tourism and textile sectors.
"Nepal welcomes wholeheartedly foreign investment and joint ventures in these fields," Foreign Minister Prakash Chandra Lohani told a Nepal-China trade and investment seminar.
The seminar coincided with the first meeting of the Nepal-China Non-governmental Cooperation Forum, set up six months ago to bring businesses from the two countries together.
Nepalese businessmen said China could invest in production of low-cost goods in Nepal for export to third countries.

The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), which groups Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, last year adopted the South Asian Preferential Trading Arrangement.
They aim to establish a free-trade area by 2005.
Chinese businessmen said they were interested in doing business with neighbouring states.

"We firmly believe that the mutual complements and increasing mutual connections among China, South Asia and Southeast Asia will help to bring about fruitful results of our cooperation," said Liu Yonghao, director of the Private Entrepreneurs Delegation of Chinese Industry and Commerce Association.
"We will try our best to realize this target," Liu said.
Nepali officials said they want foreign investment in hydro-electric power for export primarily to neighbouring India, with which it suffers a $306.6 million trade deficit.
The Himalayan kingdom has the potential to generate up to 83,000 megawatts of hydroelectric power, which would make it one of the world's top producers.
It currently generates only 293 megawatts of electricity and only 15 percent of its people -- among the world's poorest -- have access to electricity.
